geometry_gate.proposed_contract: For each present entry, widen ordinal arithmetic, require each axis start to be inside the tile and use full interior or true-edge dimensions. Whole chunks outside a crop may be omitted. This is a proposed tightening, not proof that all external or deployed encoders conform. It does not establish tile/bounds intersection or all coverage.
geometry_gate.wire_shape_tradeoff: The original gate author recommended checking declared width and height as producer-shape assertions and using one derived operational geometry. The author later challenged that recommendation: the tracked builder computes each dimension once for both encoding and declarations, so they are not independent observations. The revised recommendation removes the derivable fields in a clean schema, derives checked geometry, and checks decoded length before returning a cell. A retained checked assertion instead offers earlier detection of an honestly mismatched declaration. Field removal changes schema, package identities, producers and consumers, and can defer a short-payload failure until decode. Neither alternative can establish actual row order from flat bytes; a same-area transposition is not detected by length alone. Central policy, historical closure and future acceptance remain open.
geometry_gate.precedence: For a retained-assertion design, a separate geometry pass after the complete existing load-stage integrity, range and index passes can preserve those checks' relative precedence. Inserting geometry validation into the per-entry index loop could preempt a later duplicate-key or inconsistent-tile error. Either eager geometry check moves failure ahead of a later lazy decode error. Field removal changes parsing and identity and needs its own precedence review.

These are proposals, not executed tests.
